pool.text: King David I granted a toft in burgo meo de Edenesburg to the Priory of Dunfermline.
Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh was established by royal charter in fifteen hundred six.
King James VI and I gave the town council a royal charter permitting university establishment.
The University of Edinburgh was established by royal charter in fifteen eighty-three.
King James VI succeeded to the English throne, uniting the crowns of Scotland and England.
An act of parliament created the High Constables of Edinburgh to keep order.
Edinburgh's Orthodox synagogue opened in Salisbury Road to accommodate a congregation.
The City of Edinburgh entered into fourteen international twinning arrangements starting from nineteen fifty-four.
A green belt encircling Edinburgh was designated, stretching from Dalmeny to Prestongrange.
Heriot-Watt University was granted university status by royal charter in nineteen sixty-six.
Edinburgh served as the venue hosting the Eurovision Song Contest.
Napier College was renamed Napier Polytechnic in nineteen eighty-six.
The Edinburgh Diamond Devils baseball club won its first Scottish Championship as Reivers in nineteen ninety-one.
Edinburgh Napier University gained university status in nineteen ninety-two.
Edinburgh's Old and New Towns were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Scotland Act was passed establishing a devolved Scottish Parliament and Scottish Executive.
The baseball club adopted its present name of Edinburgh Diamond Devils in nineteen ninety-nine.
The medical school moved to purpose-built accommodation adjacent to the new Royal Infirmary in two thousand and two.
Edinburgh Park station opened to serve the Gyle business park and headquarters.
The Edinburgh Marathon has been held annually in the city since two thousand and three.
